chunks: 1786 - And in the narration of Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:

“The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله fasted so much that it was said: he does not break the fast. Then he broke the fast so much that it was said: he does not fast. Then he fasted the fast of Dāwūd عليه السلام, one day and one day. Then he was taken عليه السلام while observing the fast of three days in the month, and he said: ‘They equal the fasting of a lifetime and remove the distress of the chest.’”
And Ḥammād said: al-waḥar means whispering.
Then Ḥammād said: So I said: which days are they? He said: “The first Thursday in the month, the first Wednesday after the tenth of it, and the last Thursday in it.”

I said: And how did these become the days that are fasted? He said: “Because those before us among the nations, when punishment descended upon one of them, it descended on these days. So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله fasted these days because they are the feared days.”

key_terms.ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ: three days of fasting in each month
key_terms.صَوْمَ الدَّهْرِ: fasting for a lifetime in reward and equivalence
key_terms.صَوْمَ دَاوُدَ: the pattern of fasting every other day associated with Prophet Dāwūd عليه السلام
key_terms.وَحَرِ الصَّدْرِ: the distress or troubling agitation of the chest

ai.seo_question: Which three days of the month are recommended for fasting in this hadith, and why were they chosen?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the fasting practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, showing that he observed different patterns before settling on fasting three days each month. It highlights the merit of these days, stating that they equal lifelong fasting in reward and help remove inner whisperings, while also identifying the specific days and their historical significance.
